owner_words: I think we should do that. What I want is a single 64-bit build that will work on any 64-bit PC.
target: One x86-64 PC release/build pipeline,one canonical native64-bit OS payload,BIOS and UEFI entry loaders.
payload_identity: Both firmware entries must load the identical compiled OS payload;verify hashes and common handoff behavior.
packaging: Aim for one primary dual-firmware boot image;any additional media wrappers retain the same payload and release identity.
bootstrap_modes: Firmware startup modes may vary;the running OS is native x86-64. No separate BIOS OS and UEFI OS editions.
coverage_policy: Publish tested CPU/firmware/device profiles and gaps;boot-method support alone is not universal hardware compatibility.
current_pc_release_support: UEFI-only original PC image;source-pinned existing qualifications
firmware_bitness_inventory: pending;do not equate CPU width with firmware ABI
hardware_work: display adapters and common framebuffer description
first_engineering_step: Inventory UEFI coupling;freeze firmware-independent payload handoff,ownership and boot-media/source prerequisites.
immediate_checkpoint: paired-native-preview-2 unchanged;BIOS not newly required for provisional ROM0.4.0-alpha.1/PC0.2.0-alpha.1
display: Original monochrome512x342 logical scene,unscaled and centered on supported larger PC framebuffers.
native_parity: Shared native68000/x86 features and PC legacy68k compatibility retained;external native-application gate unchanged.
workers: Small lead decision/record task;qualifications reused. No new quota/savings claims;remaining external allowances unavailable.
